## reasoning ##
1. The workload is TPC-C with 16 concurrent sessions on only 4 vCPUs, so the configuration prioritizes short OLTP transactions and avoids JIT compilation and parallel-query startup overhead.
2. The observed planner, parser, and executor overhead supports disabling JIT, forced parallelism, diagnostic statistics, plan printing, and disconnection logging.
3. shared_buffers is raised to approximately 7.7 GiB, while effective_cache_size is set near 23.1 GiB to represent PostgreSQL buffers plus the likely operating-system cache without consuming all 30.82 GiB of RAM.
4. work_mem is increased conservatively because it is allocated per operation and potentially per parallel worker; the selected value improves sorts and hashes without creating excessive aggregate memory exposure across 16 sessions.
5. A larger max_wal_size reduces checkpoint frequency and associated buffer/WAL contention during the write-intensive TPC-C workload.
6. synchronous_commit is disabled to reduce commit-path latency and XLogFlush pressure, while fsync remains enabled so PostgreSQL still flushes WAL asynchronously; this improves throughput but can lose recently acknowledged transactions after an operating-system or power failure.
7. commit_delay and commit_siblings are assigned non-boundary values, although commit grouping has limited effect while synchronous_commit is disabled.
8. Parallel plans are discouraged using force_parallel_mode=off, one worker per gather, and elevated parallel cost estimates because parallel setup is generally counterproductive for short OLTP statements on four vCPUs.
9. cursor_tuple_fraction is moved toward complete-result consumption, while remaining strictly inside its numeric range; this is expected to have little effect unless the benchmark uses SQL cursors.
10. A nonzero idle transaction timeout prevents abandoned transactions from retaining locks and snapshots, but is long enough not to interrupt normal benchmark transactions.
11. zero_damaged_pages remains disabled because enabling it can conceal storage corruption, and all debug and per-stage statistics switches remain disabled to eliminate avoidable hot-path overhead.
12. The target TPS cannot be guaranteed from one prior observation and no matching historical rules, so this configuration should be validated through repeated warm-cache TPC-C runs using identical durability, checkpoint, and client conditions.
